title: Wave Patterns
subject: science
tagline: Spot amplitude, frequency, and energy in motion.

lessons.title: What waves carry
lessons.summary: Waves move energy — the water (or air) mostly stays put.

steps.title: Energy travels, matter mostly nods
steps.body: At a stadium, the wave rolls around the stands while people only stand and sit. Sound and ocean ripples work the same idea: a disturbance travels, carrying energy through a medium.
steps.callout: Ask: what is moving forward — the stuff, or the pattern?

steps.prompt: In a sound wave moving across a room, what mainly travels from speaker to ear?

options.label: A wind of air molecules racing across the room

steps.hint: Air jiggles in place; the disturbance propagates.
steps.success: Energy rides the pattern. The air is the medium, not the traveler.

steps.prompt: Match each wave idea to its everyday meaning.

pairs.right: How tall / intense the wave is

steps.hint: Tallness, timing, and spacing are three different knobs.
steps.success: Those three knobs describe most simple waves.

steps.prompt: Order these sound pitches from lowest frequency to highest.
steps.hint: Higher pitch means peaks arrive more often.
steps.success: Frequency is the hidden clock behind pitch.

lessons.title: Energy and size
lessons.summary: Bigger amplitude usually means more energy in the wave.

steps.title: Louder is often larger swings
steps.body: Turning up a speaker increases amplitude: air compressions get stronger. The note can stay the same frequency while the energy in each swing grows.

steps.prompt: Which changes usually increase a wave’s energy?

options.label: Keeping amplitude tiny while changing color labels
Drawing the wave with a thicker pencil only

steps.hint: Ignore drawing tricks. Think physical intensity and rate.
steps.success: Amplitude and frequency both shape the energy story.

steps.prompt: A wave has frequency 5 Hz. How many full cycles happen in 3 seconds?
